
SHOW-WORK-UNIT
Display detailed information about a work unit including Example Mapping data, dependencies, and linked feature files

WHEN TO USE
  Use to view complete details of a work unit: status, type, description, Example Mapping (rules, examples, questions, assumptions), dependencies (blocks/blockedBy/dependsOn/relatesTo), linked feature files, attachments, and system reminders. Supports both human-readable text and JSON output.

PREREQUISITES
  • Work unit must exist in spec/work-units.json

USAGE
  fspec show-work-unit <workUnitId> [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <workUnitId> (required)
    Work unit ID (e.g., AUTH-001)

OPTIONS
  -f, --format <format>
    Output format: text (default) or json

COMMON PATTERNS
  • View work unit before Example Mapping session
    Example: # Check current state
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001

# Add rules/examples/questions
fspec add-rule AUTH-001 "Must validate email"
fspec add-example AUTH-001 "User with valid credentials"
fspec add-question AUTH-001 "Should we support OAuth?" --human
    undefined

  • Export work unit data for processing
    Example: # Export as JSON for scripts/tools
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001 --format json > auth-001.json

# Process with jq
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001 --format json | jq .rules
    undefined

  • Check system reminders
    Example: # View work unit to see reminders
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001

# Output includes:
# <system-reminder>
# Missing estimate for work unit AUTH-001
# </system-reminder>
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. List work units: fspec list-work-units → 2. Show details: fspec show-work-unit <workUnitId> → 3. Update fields: fspec update-work-unit <workUnitId> --title "New title" → 4. Verify changes: fspec show-work-unit <workUnitId>

EXAMPLES
  1. Show work unit details in text format
  $ fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001
  AUTH-001
Type: story
Status: specifying

User login feature
Implement user authentication

Rules:
  1. Must validate email format
  2. Password must be 8+ characters

Questions:
  [0] Should we support OAuth?

Linked Features:
  spec/features/auth/login.feature
    spec/features/auth/login.feature:10 - Valid user login

Created: 13/10/2025 14:30:00
Updated: 13/10/2025 15:45:00

  2. Show work unit details as JSON
  $ fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001 --format json
  {
  "id": "AUTH-001",
  "title": "User login feature",
  "type": "story",
  "status": "specifying",
  "description": "Implement user authentication",
  "rules": ["Must validate email format"],
  "questions": ["[0] Should we support OAuth?"],
  "linkedFeatures": [...],
  "createdAt": "2025-10-13T14:30:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-10-13T15:45:00Z"
}

  3. Show epic details with children
  $ fspec show-work-unit EPIC-001
  EPIC-001
Type: epic
Status: implementing

User Management

Children: AUTH-001, AUTH-002, AUTH-003

Created: 01/10/2025 10:00:00

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Work unit 'AUTH-999' does not exist
    Fix: Verify the work unit ID exists with: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ ENOENT: no such file or directory, spec/work-units.json
    Fix: Initialize work units with: fspec create-story PREFIX "title" (or create-bug/create-task)

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec list-work-units
  fspec update-work-unit
  fspec update-work-unit-status
  fspec add-rule
  fspec add-example
  fspec add-question
  fspec dependencies

NOTES
  • Text format shows all Example Mapping data (rules, examples, questions, assumptions, architecture notes)
  • Text format shows all dependency relationships (blocks, blockedBy, dependsOn, relatesTo)
  • Text format shows linked feature files with scenario names and line numbers
  • JSON format includes all fields, suitable for scripting and automation
  • System reminders are displayed for missing estimates, empty Example Mapping, long phase duration, or large estimates (> 13 points for story/bug)
  • Questions are filtered to show only unselected questions (answered questions are hidden)
  • Linked features are automatically discovered by scanning feature files for work unit tags
